BRODU_2011.citation: Nicolas Brodu, Reconstruction of Epsilon-Machines in Predictive Frameworks and Decisional States, Advances in Complex Systems 14(5):761-794, 2011, DOI 10.1142/S0219525911003347, arXiv:0902.0600
BRODU_2011.structural_note: Paper contains NO numbered definitions/theorems/propositions; only numbered display equations are Eq.(1) Sec.3.1 and Eq.(2) Sec.4.2. Locations are section + run-in label anchors. arXiv v5 (author-final) and author PDF textually consistent; published full text 403-unreachable.

causal_state_equivalence_brodu.location: Sec. 3.2, run-in block 'Causal state equivalence relation:' (light-cone prose version Sec. 2.1)
causal_state_equivalence_brodu.assumptions: causal (not merely predictive) reading: X restricted to past, Z to future (Sec. 2.1 caveat)
causal_state_equivalence_brodu.quote: x1 =c x2 iff the conditional distributions P(Z|x1)=P(Z|x2) are the same

iso_prediction_definition.location: Sec. 3.2, run-in block 'Prediction equivalence relation:' + partitions sentence defining psi in Psi
iso_prediction_definition.assumptions: expected utility U(y|x) well-defined; each y_x chosen independently per x
iso_prediction_definition.quote: x1 =p x2 iff argmax_y U(y|x1)=argmax_y U(y|x2)

iso_utility_definition_brodu.location: Sec. 3.2, run-in block 'Utility equivalence relation:' + partitions sentence defining upsilon in Upsilon
iso_utility_definition_brodu.assumptions: utility U(y,z) defined on Z^2, independent of x (Sec. 3.1)
iso_utility_definition_brodu.quote: x1 =u x2 iff max_y U(y|x1)=max_y U(y|x2)

decisional_state_definition.location: Sec. 3.2, paragraph after the upsilon/psi partitions sentence ('Let us call decisional states...')
decisional_state_definition.assumptions: utility encodes all the user needs for the decision; deciding does not modify the system
decisional_state_definition.quote: decisional states omega in Omega are the intersection of both equivalence relations

causal_refines_decisional.location: Sec. 3.3 closing sentences (Fig. 2); echoed Sec. 3.5 bullet 1 and Sec. 5.4
causal_refines_decisional.quote: the causal states sub-partition both the iso-utility, iso-prediction and decisional states; the converse is not true

decisional_complexity.location: Sec. 3.4 prose paragraph defining D=I(x;omega); local D_omega=-log2 p(omega) same paragraph; literal 'D=H(omega)' only in Sec. 5.4 (Occam bullet)
decisional_complexity.quote: D=I(x;omega); D<=C in the discrete case

transition_graph.location: Sec. 3.4, paragraph 'Let x be the current system configuration...' (Fig. 3; algorithm recap Fig. 4 step 9, Sec. 5.1)
transition_graph.assumptions: discrete scenario with alphabet A; coarser states are unions of epsilon-machine causal states
transition_graph.quote: p(e_{omega->gamma}) = sum_{x in omega} sum_{a in A} p(xa in gamma | x in omega)

determinism_recursive_sufficiency.location: Sec. 3.4 paragraphs after the transition-probability definition incl. footnote 4; Sec. 5.5; Sec. 6.1 opening; Sec. 3.5 bullet 3
determinism_recursive_sufficiency.assumptions: discrete case; sub-machine claim rests on Shalizi's hypothesis [24, sec. 11.2.2]
determinism_recursive_sufficiency.quote: we loose the Markov property of the coarser graph; symbol labels lost at the coarser level; 'recursively sufficient' does not appear in the paper

experiment_comparison.source: projecteuclid full texts (OCR-verified verbatim, header-pinned pages)

deficiency_comparison.location: Le Cam 1964, Definition 8, Sec. 4 'Approximate sufficiency', p. 1429 (epsilon-deficiency); Definition 9 p. 1433 (delta(E,F) as inf over positive normalized linear maps of sup_theta norm of MP_theta - Q_theta); Theorem 3, Sec. 4, pp. 1430-1431 (equivalence of randomized-map, deficiency, risk-set and per-procedure risk conditions; epsilon=0 case noted as 'essentially a form of the Blackwell-Sherman-Stein theorem'); Proposition 8 p. 1433; Le Cam 1986 Ch. 2 'Some Results from Decision Theory: Deficiencies' pp. 16-28, Sec. 3 'Deficiencies; Distances' pp. 18-23, Ch. 2 Theorem 2; Ch. 3 Sec. 7 'The Blackwell-Sherman-Stein Theorem' p. 43
deficiency_comparison.assumptions: arbitrary parameter space; all decision spaces; finite-support priors (Def 8); L-space framework (Def 9)
deficiency_comparison.source: projecteuclid 1964 full text (OCR-verified) + Springer 1986 TOC/front matter

LSS_2001.citation: Littman, Sutton & Singh, Predictive Representations of State, NIPS 2001 (Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 14), pp. 1555-1561; ACM DL 10.5555/2980539.2980741
LSS_2001.structural_note: papers.nips.cc metadata lists only Littman & Sutton; the PDF title block lists all three authors. Pagination verified via ACM DL and S. Singh's Michigan NIPS page.

psr_predictive_state.location: Sec. 1 'Predictive State Representations': prediction vector p(h) is a PSR iff it is a sufficient statistic, P(t|h) = f_t(p(h)), Eq. (1); linear PSR P(t|h) = p(h) m_t, Eq. (2); recursive state update Eq. (3); Theorem 1 (finite-POMDP-representable environment has a linear PSR with no more tests than minimal-POMDP states), proof in Sec. 2 incl. Lemma 1
psr_predictive_state.assumptions: discrete-observation environment indexed by history h; tests t = sets of future observation-event sequences; Theorem 1 requires finite-POMDP representability

OSBAND_2023.citation: Osband, Wen, Asghari, Dwaracherla, Ibrahimi, Lu & Van Roy, Epistemic Neural Networks, NeurIPS 2023; arXiv:2107.08924 (v1 2021-07-19, v8 2023-05-17)
OSBAND_2023.structural_note: Theorem 2 is labeled [informal] by the authors (formal version in Appendix B); dyadic sampling (Appendix E) is explicitly 'a practical heuristic' with no theorem.

enn_joint_predictive.location: Sec. 3 'Epistemic neural networks': ENN = function class f + reference distribution P_Z, output f_theta(x,z) with epistemic index z; joint prediction Eq. (2): integral over P_Z(dz) of the product of softmax(f_theta(x_t,z))_{y_t}, contrasted with marginal product Eq. (1); Theorem 2 [informal] Sec. 3.1 (small expected joint log loss implies near-optimal actions for any decision problem; formal in Appendix B); Theorem 3 Sec. 3.2 (every BNN expressible as an ENN, strict converse fails); Theorem 4 Sec. 4.3 p. 7 (linear-Gaussian epinet with LSG loss Eq. 9 converges in distribution to the exact posterior as D_Z grows; proof Appendix D)
enn_joint_predictive.assumptions: z iid across inputs; Theorem 4 assumes linear-Gaussian data model + linear-Gaussian epinet + Gaussian bootstrapping contexts

SC_2001.citation: Shalizi & Crutchfield, Computational Mechanics: Pattern and Prediction, Structure and Simplicity, Journal of Statistical Physics 104(3/4):817-860, 2001; arXiv:cond-mat/9907176

causal_state_equivalence.location: Definition 5 ('A Process's Causal States'), Sec IV.A 'Causal States': causal states = range of the map E, E(s-) = {s-' : P(S+ in S+ | S- = s-) = P(S+ in S+ | S- = s-')}; equivalence-relation form stated immediately after (noted as 'the original approach', their ref. 6)
causal_state_equivalence.assumptions: stationary stochastic process; futures measurable w.r.t. the sigma-algebra of S+; cardinality/topology of the causal-state set unspecified

causal_state_minimality.location: Theorem 2 ('Causal States Are Minimal'), Sec V, using Definition 11 ('Prescient Rivals') and Lemma 7 ('Refinement Lemma'); supporting: Theorem 1 + Corollary 1 ('Maximally Prescient' / 'Sufficient Statistics') and Theorem 3 ('Unique'), all Sec V
causal_state_minimality.assumptions: rival partitions must be prescient; minimality measured via the statistical complexity of the rival
